A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same TP-as-a-Judge/RLTPF work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite renumbering and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training results across eight mathematical benchmarks, verification experiments, training ablations and repeated-run results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds iteration-length statistics, component error rates and further verification examples.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 and Algorithm 1 retain question generation, four-phase question formalisation, iterative Lean verification and SFT followed by DPO. Appendix K illustrates the existing procedure without introducing a new algorithm component or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3,508-sample SIMQA dataset derived from GSM8K/MATH and the same eight evaluation benchmarks. The added property-sale example remains within the existing mathematical word-problem coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 retain the same prompting, trained-model, mathematical-specialist and GPT/judge comparisons. The training-strategy comparators also remain unchanged in v1 Table 6 and v2 Table 7. Appendix G does not report an evaluated CoMAT-removal baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 adds manual inspection of ten randomly sampled examples and analysis of token length by iteration. These introduce limited diagnostic procedures; the existing benchmark settings, decoding, model configurations, training budgets and answer-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends existing analyses with inspection of syntax/tactic failures, sequence length by iteration, and a component error breakdown. Appendices J/K add a paired verification case and its debugging trace. The existing training ablation is retained; the asserted approximately 20% CoMAT benefit lacks a reported controlled ablation.

E5.justification: Appendix C retains three runs using seeds 42, 2103 and 1234, with the same mean and standard-deviation reporting for Llama-3.1 and Llama-3.2. No additional uncertainty estimates, significance tests or repeated-run procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports average sequence lengths of 731.2, 869.1, 937.6, 1134.6 and 1343.0 tokens across iterations 1–5. Table 11 adds question-stage error rates of 13.10% for autoformalisation and 10.00% for alignment checks. The paired property-sale case adds False/Verified outcomes. All matched benchmark, ablation, confusion-matrix and seed-result entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix K adds example-level formal definitions and derivations for the property-sale problem, including an exact rational selling price, a profit identity and successive Lean proof attempts. The general mathematical definitions and assumptions underlying the method remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: iterative autoformalisation, TP-as-a-Judge and RLTPF. The execution-rate improvement from 60% to 87% and data-efficiency claims using 3,508 samples are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets longer sequences and additional iterations as accommodating more complex reasoning and potentially reducing bias toward easier instances. Appendix G expands explanations of CoMAT and alignment checks as safeguards for data quality. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement with a repository pointer and an illustrative Lean-code/error-output trace in Appendix K. These extend implementation documentation; generation parameters, training hyperparameters, hardware and dataset-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Muennighoff et al. on s1, Li et al. on symbolic equivalence and semantic consistency, and Poiroux et al. on type checking. These support limited additional discussion. Numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works, including Lego-Prover.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, adds acknowledgements and explanatory passages, inserts Appendix G and appends Appendix K. Former Appendices G–I become H–J. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two diagnostic tables and boxed case, Lean-code and error-output displays. Existing tables receive formatting or placement changes, including the confusion matrix and appendix tables. The existing figures and basic document layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The code-access statement, diagnostic tables and worked Lean repair trace make the verification pipeline easier to inspect while preserving the original experimental evidence. The gains are limited: Appendix G asserts an approximately 20% CoMAT benefit without a reported ablation, and the new complexity interpretation relies on token length. Overall, the added transparency provides a modest quality improvement.
